questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Language spoken and quality of universities

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Melbourne is an extremely nice city, best for night life and live music in AU. Wont make you as poor as Sydney. Downside is the weather can be quite bad.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, UniMelb was quite good at letting you know where to go and what to do.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Information letters

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: My opinion was as long as you can pay the same prices as in Copenhagen and dont want to live in the CBD area, but around campus you should be fine. Finding accommodation when you have arrived already and want to move together with people you have met can be quite difficult.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The official accom UniMelb suggests is extremely overpriced. Some nice locations but you can definitely do better with some research.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Straight forward

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They essentially just want some basic details and proof of english knowledge etc. and after that you can directly go to choose courses. Very flexible as well, especially when compared to KU. You are able to completely change courses until like 4 weeks after semester start.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Their support and other students.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Easily done

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just make sure to do it before due dates

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I personally didnt have many problems. But UniMelb is ranked quite poorly by their students. Their organisation is not the best.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Very much depends on what you take. If you take 4 high BA level bachelor subjects you're not going to have a great time. It can be very time consuming. If you take into courses you probably wont have much of a problem. People generally say it is way easier in AU to pass than at KU. Specifically for UniMelb I would not say this to be true for Computer Science at least. (But as I said depends on what you choose).

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More professional, higher quality TA's. You notice they have more money for acquiring workforce.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Cryptography and Security, Principles of Marketing, Principles of Management and Graphics and Interaction

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The principle courses are dead easy. Graphics and interaction is a good course, group based though which can lead to annoyances. Cryptography and Security is the most time consuming course I have ever taken, don't take this if you want to enjoy your time.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Anything alcohol related is extremely expensive. Tram prices are what you make them. Free in the CBD, outside you can tap on. If you do its very expensive. Food is way cheaper than in copenhagen

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Veggies are expensive

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Idk I never really ended up going to much club stuff. Surf club is very overbooked and chances are slim for you to join their trips. Everything else is nice if you find it interesting. They have something for everyone if you have the time to go.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything you'd want

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Personal preference

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Phillip Island, Wilsons Promotory, Great Ocean Road, Footy or any sports activities and the MCG. Go to bars and Cafes as much as possible.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Not hard at all, quite like home but people are way more relaxed, open and nice

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Chances are you wont meet too many local students

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Standing on the left side on escalators like broooo

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Very relaxed

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Enjoy your time even while Uni is going on. It is over faster than you expect. 

Taking 4 courses on a 3rd year level for a bachelor that isnt easy can be quite literally impossible. (Especially true for hard master courses)

Expect really bad weather especially when you arrive in winter. Melbourne summer starts after their Semester 2. Which means in December / January. Dont expect much before. Arctic winds are incredibly cold.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting people from all parts of the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Moving away from everyone you know could be difficult for some

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: naa

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
